original_test_intent: Verify CPU performance-state response to BIOS Turbo Mode by showing frequency above approved base under controlled stress when Enabled and constrained to the approved non-turbo behavior when Disabled, subject to owner resolution of the contradictory second criterion.
original_method: A qualified operator records the initial BIOS state, sets Enabled and Disabled one at a time with save/reset and boot confirmation; for each state run the same bounded CPU workload and collect full per-socket/core time-series frequency, driver/governor, thermal, power-limit and throttle evidence; compare to an approved base-frequency rule and restore the final recipe setting.
manual_activity: The owner corrects Criterion 2 and approves base-frequency semantics, workload/sampling, maintenance/recovery and final setting; an operator performs both BIOS transitions and confirms boot; the owner decides the verdict.

Authoritative base frequency, allowed disabled-state variation and enabled-state exceedance rule
Approved stress tool, workload, duration, affinity and frequency sample cadence
Frequency tool/field mapping plus governor/driver, power-limit, temperature and throttle context
Console/BIOS access, maintenance window, recovery and approved final setting

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use operator-controlled BIOS transitions and identical controlled workloads with time-series frequency and limiting-condition evidence across the full CPU topology.

modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Frequency varies by active-core count, workload, thermals and power limits; the owner must define aggregation and tolerance rather than expect a constant exact value.

review_improvement: Preserves the Enabled/Disabled criteria contradiction, converts PARTIAL into an approved hybrid class, removes insecure static shortcuts and requires full workload-dependent evidence with recovery/restoration.
independent_technical_reasoning: P-state behavior is dynamic: lscpu or cpupower limits describe available policy but do not show actual frequency under load. Turbo boost depends on active-core count and thermal/power headroom, while disabled frequency may not be numerically constant at base across every sample. Therefore the owner must define time-series aggregation and tolerances, and the contradictory second criterion must remain pending rather than being silently corrected.
